old: Continuous self-pollination causes inbreeding depression, so plants have outbreeding devices. In some species pollen release and stigma receptivity are not synchronised. In others the anther and stigma are placed at different positions. Self-incompatibility is a genetic mechanism that stops pollen of the same flower from germinating or growing. Unisexual flowers also help. In monoecious plants such as castor and maize, autogamy is prevented but geitonogamy is not. In dioecious plants such as papaya, both autogamy and geitonogamy are prevented. Pollen-pistil interaction is the dynamic process by which the pistil recognises compatible pollen through chemical components of the pollen and the pistil. Compatible pollen germinates, and the pollen tube grows through a germ pore, down the stigma and style, and enters the ovule through the micropyle. It then enters one synergid through the filiform apparatus. Plant breeders use artificial hybridization, which involves emasculation (removing anthers from bisexual flowers before dehiscence) followed by bagging.
new: Continuous self-pollination causes inbreeding depression, so plants have outbreeding devices. In some species pollen release and stigma receptivity are not synchronised. In others the anther and stigma are placed at different positions. Self-incompatibility is a genetic mechanism that prevents self-pollen (from the same flower or other flowers of the same plant) from fertilising the ovules, by inhibiting pollen germination or pollen tube growth in the pistil. Unisexual flowers also help. In monoecious plants such as castor and maize, autogamy is prevented but geitonogamy is not. In dioecious plants such as papaya, both autogamy and geitonogamy are prevented. Pollen-pistil interaction is the dynamic process by which the pistil recognises compatible pollen through chemical components of the pollen and the pistil. Compatible pollen germinates, and the pollen tube grows through a germ pore, down the stigma and style, and enters the ovule through the micropyle. It then enters one synergid through the filiform apparatus. Plant breeders use artificial hybridization, which involves emasculation (removing anthers from bisexual flowers before dehiscence) followed by bagging.
fixes: Self-incompatibility blocks self-pollen from the same flower or other flowers of the same plant, not just the same flower
